identity.title: Retrieval Head Mechanistically Explains Long-Context Factuality

problem.claim: Explain how transformer-based long-context models retrieve relevant information from arbitrary context locations.

gap.claim: The mechanism underlying this retrieval capability remains elusive.

contributions.claim: A systematic investigation identifies a special attention-head type, termed retrieval heads, as largely responsible for information retrieval.
The paper reports that retrieval heads are universal, sparse, intrinsic to short-context pretraining, and dynamically activated across contexts.
The paper examines retrieval-head influence on retrieval, hallucination, chain-of-thought reasoning, and intrinsic-knowledge answering.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce and characterize the concept of retrieval heads as the internal component responsible for seeking information from input tokens.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across a wide spectrum of explored models, all models with long-context capability reportedly contain retrieval heads, comprising less than 5% of attention heads.
For Llama-2 7B, the authors report that 12 retrieval heads always attend to required information despite context changes, while other retrieval heads activate in different contexts.

The authors report that pruning retrieval heads causes retrieval failure and hallucination, whereas pruning random non-retrieval heads does not affect retrieval ability; masking retrieval heads also more strongly impacts CoT than intrinsic-knowledge answering.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-context models can retrieve information, but the underlying mechanism is unclear.
A systematic model investigation identifies sparse attention heads associated with retrieval.
The heads are reported to persist from short-context pretraining, remain involved after context extension, and vary in activation by context.
Pruning and masking results connect retrieval heads to retrieval, hallucination, and CoT reasoning, with weaker impact on intrinsic-knowledge answering.
The observations are presented as a mechanistic explanation and motivation for future work on hallucination, reasoning, and KV-cache compression.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a proposed internal mechanism with both structural properties and targeted interventions, including pruning retrieval versus random non-retrieval heads.

lessons.interpretation: Mechanistic claims become more informative when identification and intervention are presented together.
lessons.application: For a mechanism paper, pair a component-discovery analysis with an intervention that selectively tests the component against a matched control.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when interventions are unavailable, confounded, or cannot isolate the proposed component.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the full model set, retrieval tasks, pruning protocol, or quantitative effect sizes.
The stated causal effects and broad mechanistic interpretation are author-reported and cannot be independently assessed from the abstract alone.
It is unclear how retrieval heads were operationally identified and how CoT and intrinsic-knowledge tasks were controlled or measured.
